reuses.lift_trend: logger.progress_signals (4-week window, >= 3 sessions over >= 14 days, up > +0.5 %/wk, dropping < -1.0 %/wk)

progress.weeks: Weeks start Monday (local). The in-progress week is never used for trends or refinements.

weekly_sets.plan: routine planned sets x rating (rating >= 0.25), summed over the routine days (no hard-set credit discount)

trend.rule: last 4 completed weeks, weeks with no completed session left out; >= 3 weeks needed. Least-squares slope of actual sets vs week index, as % of the mean: up > +5 %/wk, down < -5 %/wk, else flat; mean 0 -> flat.

main_lift.rule: Among exercises with a progress_signals trend in the window and rating[m] >= 0.5: type primary first, then accessory, then isolation; then the higher rating; then more sessions; then id. Reports first and last e1RM in the window, %/week and status.

adherence.rule: Sum completed_analytics adherence over the last 4 completed weeks: sets_ratio = completed planned sets / planned sets; sessions_ratio = completed / (completed + skipped). Per muscle: sum actual / sum plan over the weeks that had a completed session.

notes.rule: For exercises with rating[m] >= 0.5: Always notes = history.exNotes[exercise] (sticky), This session notes = entries[].notes of completed sessions. Always notes first (exercise id order), then This session notes newest first; at most 3 in total.

guards.rule: No refinement fires before 4 completed sessions spanning 2+ weeks. Each refinement has its own minimum below. One workout never triggers anything.

stall.rule: Per routine exercise: its last 4+ non-deload exposures (sessions with a valid e1RM) span >= 21 days, and the best e1RM of the last 3 is not above the best before them x (1 + review.flat_pct/100).
stall.rep_range_change: median top-set reps of the last 3 exposures vs the midpoint of rep_range(exercise, goal): midpoint = floor((low + high) / 2); at or below it -> suggest midpoint .. high, above it -> low .. midpoint. Display only; no board edit (the rep range is a target, not a tile field). Time-based ranges (holds) get no rep change.
stall.swap_variation: first tools/swap.py swaps(id, n=40) candidate that is eligible for the exercise's own template slot (tools/templates.py eligible(rule_for(id), level): same slot, type, movement_pattern and, for isolation, primary muscle; level filters) and not already in the routine, same equipment family first (swap.fam), -> {op: swap} on every routine tile of the exercise, same sets.

missed_sets.rule: Per routine exercise: of the last 3 completed sessions that planned it (session snapshot), at least 2 have fewer done working sets than planned (a skipped entry counts 0).
missed_sets.trim_sets: set the routine tile to max(2, round(mean done over those sessions)), only if lower than planned -> {op: sets}.
missed_sets.move_sets: move the trimmed sets (at least 2) to the routine day that lacks the exercise and was completed most often in the last 4 completed weeks (then fewest sets, then week order) -> {op: sets} + {op: add}; offered only when it adds no non-info flag (fix_validation).

under_delivered.rule: Muscle with plan >= 2 sets: actual < plan x (1 - 0.25) in each of the last 2 completed weeks, each with >= 1 completed session.
under_delivered.causes: missed_sets (a missed_sets refinement on an exercise rating the muscle >= 0.5), else skipped_sessions (a skipped session in those weeks that planned an exercise rating the muscle >= 0.5), else swaps_or_logging (info only).
under_delivered.actions: missed_sets -> link to that refinement; skipped_sessions -> link to one skipped_day refinement per weekday; else no edit.

skipped_day.rule: One per routine weekday that had a skipped session behind an under_delivered muscle (the muscles are listed together, not one card each).
skipped_day.action: reschedule: move every tile of that day to the nearest empty weekday (earlier first on a tie) whose result adds no non-info flag -> {op: remove} x n + {op: add} x n; none -> info only.

make_more_efficient.label: Make it more efficient
make_more_efficient.shows_when: any muscle-day has payoff band amber or red
make_more_efficient.goal: bring every muscle-day back to its Payoff peak (marginal >= 1) without dropping any muscle below its weekly minimum
algorithm: 1. Collect muscle-days with band amber or red. Order: red first, then larger sets_past_peak, then day mon..sun, then muscle A-Z.

2. Take the first. Candidates = tiles that day crediting the muscle. Rank with rules efficient_trim.tie_breaks (pools A/B/C; A = tiles in board order whose sets fall past peak_n, the payoff analogue of wasted_late_sets; key = lowest credit / muscle_fatigue first, then latest tile, then id).

3. Cut 1 set from the first candidate that passes efficient_trim.constraints (weekly minimum for EVERY muscle the tile credits: r2(weekly) >= volume_zones[level][m].min; min 1 set per exercise; no empty day; no new non-info flag).

4. If no cut passes: try a swap of the highest fatigue-class candidate to a lower fatigue class of the same pattern (rules fix_actions swap_exercise criteria lower_fatigue, swap.json scoring) that keeps every weekly minimum and lowers that muscle-day's k; else mark blocked.
5. Recompute and repeat until no amber/red muscle-day is left or all are blocked. Show a preview list (one line per change) before applying.
never: drop a muscle below its weekly minimum
move tiles between days (that is the per-flag fix, not this button)
make_more_efficient.reuses: rules efficient_trim (tie_breaks, constraints) with the session-limit trigger replaced by the Payoff band

push_for_max_growth.label: Push for max growth
push_for_max_growth.shows_when: any muscle is below the top of its weekly sweet spot (volume_zones[level][m].sweet[1]) and one of its days is under its cap
push_for_max_growth.goal: add sets toward each muscle's weekly sweet-spot top, never past the per-workout cap
push_for_max_growth.caps: rules session_efficiency.limits_by_goal.max_growth[level][m] (10/10/6 big/medium/small; beginner 8/8/6), compared as r1(effective sets) <= cap after the add
algorithm: 1. Muscles with r2(weekly) < sweet_top, largest gap first (then muscle A-Z).
2. Candidates = existing tiles crediting the muscle as prime (then secondary), on days where adding 1 set keeps r1(day effective sets) <= cap for EVERY muscle the tile credits.
3. Pick the day with the lowest current effective sets for the muscle, then the tile with the highest credit for it, then the lowest fatigue_per_set, then board order, then id. Add 1 set.
4. Constraints: sets_per_exercise <= 5, no new non-info flag (session_hard_sets, session_length, spinal_load), weekly r2 <= sweet_top + 0.5.
5. Repeat until no muscle below sweet_top has a feasible add. Show a preview list before applying.
